To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel framework based on the notion duality in optimization for the analysis of online learning and that the framework has led to new insights and results for online learning algorithms.

(1) we provide a new perspective for the design and understanding of online learning algorithms; (2) we derive a new universal online learning bound that is competitive with the best known bounds; (3) we show how to extend the framework to the case of non-stationary distributions; and (4) we show how the framework can be extended to handle the online convex optimization problem.

we provide a unified framework for the design of a large class of online learning algorithms that are based on the notion dual in constrained optimization, and we show that our framework is applicable to a large class of universal online learning bounds.
